# Global Systems Studio: blog summary and FAQ answers

> Educational content for U.S. persons relocating internationally. Not legal, tax, or immigration advice. Index: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/llms.txt

## Best banks for US expats opening a foreign account in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-banks-us-expats-opening-foreign-account-2026/
Published: 2026-10-14

Best banks for US expats opening a foreign account in 2026: four account types compared by who they suit, what they require and what to report.

Q: Can a US citizen open a foreign bank account?
A: Often yes, but banks set their own rules and some are cautious about US customers because of reporting obligations. Ask each bank about its policy for Americans before you apply.

Q: Do I have to report a foreign bank account to the US?
A: Possibly. FBAR is generally required when foreign accounts together exceed 10,000 US dollars at any time during the year, and Form 8938 can apply at higher thresholds. Confirm current rules with a tax professional.

Q: Can I open a foreign account before I move?
A: Sometimes. Some banks allow a start before arrival, while others need a local address or residence permit. Ask what they will accept.

Q: Should I keep my US bank account when I move abroad?
A: Many people do, for US income, taxes and bills. Ask your bank how it treats accounts with a foreign address and keep your contact details current.

Q: What documents do foreign banks usually ask for?
A: Commonly proof of address, a passport, a residence permit and sometimes a local tax number. Some documents may need translation or an apostille.

Q: Is a multi-currency account the same as a bank account?
A: Not always. Some providers are not banks, so check how funds are held and what protection applies.

Q: Can relocation coaching replace a banker or tax professional?
A: No. Global Systems Studio's ROS™ relocation coaching coordinates planning decisions; banks, qualified tax professionals and legal professionals provide advice within their respective fields.

## Best international health insurance plans for US expats 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-international-health-insurance-plans-us-expats-2026/
Published: 2026-10-14

Best international health insurance plans for US expats in 2026: five plan types compared by who they suit, what to check and where coverage gaps hide.

Q: Does Medicare cover me if I live abroad?
A: Original Medicare generally does not cover routine care outside the United States. Check current rules with Medicare or a licensed advisor before you rely on it.

Q: Do I need international insurance if my destination has public healthcare?
A: Not always, but public access can depend on residence status and waiting periods. Many expats cover the gap or add private cover for faster access.

Q: What is the difference between a US plan and an international plan?
A: US marketplace plans are built around US residence and networks. International plans are built for people who live outside their home country and may include evacuation and cover in several countries.

Q: Why is including the United States so much more expensive?
A: US medical costs are high, so insurers price US coverage accordingly. Excluding it is a common way to lower premiums, at the cost of no US cover.

Q: Will an international plan cover pre-existing conditions?
A: It depends on the insurer and how it underwrites. Some review your history and may exclude conditions; others use a moratorium. Ask for the terms in writing.

Q: Is travel insurance enough for living abroad?
A: Usually not. Travel policies are designed for trips, not residence, and often have stay limits and narrower benefits.

Q: Can relocation coaching replace an insurance broker?
A: No. Global Systems Studio's ROS™ relocation coaching coordinates planning decisions; licensed insurance, tax and legal professionals provide advice within their respective regulated fields.

## Best US expat tax preparation services in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-us-expat-tax-preparation-services-2026/
Published: 2026-10-14

Best US expat tax preparation services in 2026: five provider types compared by complexity, what each handles and what to confirm before you hire.

Q: Do I have to file US taxes if I live abroad?
A: US citizens generally must file a US return regardless of where they live, even if they owe no tax. Confirm your specific filing requirement with the IRS or a qualified professional.

Q: What is the FBAR and who must file it?
A: FBAR is a separate report of foreign financial accounts. It is generally required when foreign accounts together exceed 10,000 US dollars at any time during the year. Confirm current rules before you file.

Q: Do Americans abroad get more time to file?
A: US citizens living abroad are generally given an automatic extension to file, but any tax owed is still due on the regular deadline and interest can apply. Confirm current dates with the IRS.

Q: Is a CPA better than an enrolled agent for expat taxes?
A: Neither credential is automatically better. Look for tax experience with Americans abroad and ask who prepares and signs your return.

Q: Can I use regular tax software if I live overseas?
A: Sometimes, if your situation is simple. Foreign income and account reporting can need extra steps that mainstream software may not prompt you for.

Q: What if I have not filed for several years?
A: Speak to a qualified tax professional before filing anything. The IRS has offered procedures for eligible late filers, and which one applies depends on your facts.

Q: Can relocation coaching replace a tax preparer?
A: No. Global Systems Studio's ROS™ relocation coaching coordinates planning decisions; qualified tax, legal and financial professionals provide advice within their respective regulated fields.

## Best Caribbean countries for Americans to retire abroad in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-caribbean-countries-americans-retire-abroad-2026/
Published: 2026-10-07

Best Caribbean countries for Americans to retire abroad in 2026: Dominican Republic, Belize, Bahamas and Barbados compared by residence route, healthcare and tax.

Q: What is the best Caribbean country for Americans to retire in 2026?
A: It depends on your route, income and healthcare needs. The Dominican Republic has a retiree-specific route, Belize has a named retirement program, the Bahamas has no personal income tax, and Barbados offers familiarity.

Q: Is the Barbados Welcome Stamp good for retirees?
A: Not really. It is a 12-month remote-work permit with an income requirement and does not convert into permanent residence, so retirees typically look at other routes.

Q: Does Medicare cover me in the Caribbean?
A: Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States, apart from limited exceptions. Arrange destination coverage and medical evacuation separately.

Q: Do I still pay U.S. taxes if I retire in the Caribbean?
A: U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax filing rules wherever they live, even where there is no local personal income tax. Get cross-border tax advice for your situation.

Q: How should I plan for hurricane season?
A: Ask about insurance for the property and contents, evacuation arrangements and where you would stay during the season. Build the cost and logistics into the plan before you choose a location.

Q: Can I own property as a foreigner?
A: Rules differ by country and sometimes by property type. Confirm what foreigners may buy and what approvals are required before you commit to a purchase.

Q: Can relocation coaching replace an immigration lawyer or tax advisor?
A: No. Global Systems Studio's ROS™ relocation coaching coordinates planning decisions; qualified immigration, tax and financial professionals provide advice within their respective regulated fields.

## Best digital nomad visa countries for Americans in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-digital-nomad-visa-countries-for-americans-2026/
Published: 2026-10-07

Best digital nomad visa countries for Americans in 2026: Spain, Portugal, Greece, Costa Rica and Mexico compared by income threshold, length, tax and next steps.

Q: What is the best digital nomad visa for Americans in 2026?
A: It depends on your income, work structure and plans. Spain suits those who want a path beyond year one, Portugal suits higher documented income, and Mexico suits those who want a lower threshold close to home.

Q: How much income do I need for a digital nomad visa?
A: Reported thresholds in 2026 range from a few hundred to several thousand euros a month, and many European routes sit above 2,800 euros. Confirm the current figure with the official source because they change.

Q: Do I still pay U.S. taxes on a digital nomad visa?
A: U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax filing rules wherever they live. A visa does not change that, and local tax residence can also arise, so get cross-border tax advice.

Q: Can I work for a U.S. employer on a digital nomad visa?
A: Most routes are designed for work for employers or clients outside the country. Confirm how your arrangement would be assessed, especially if you are a contractor.

Q: Can I bring my family?
A: Often yes, but with higher income or savings expectations. Costa Rica, for example, reportedly expects more for families than for individuals.

Q: Can a digital nomad visa lead to permanent residence?
A: Some routes can count toward longer-term residence over several years and others cannot. Check whether time on the visa counts and what else is required.

Q: Can relocation coaching replace an immigration lawyer or tax advisor?
A: No. Global Systems Studio's ROS™ relocation coaching coordinates planning decisions; qualified immigration, tax and financial professionals provide advice within their respective regulated fields.

## Best golden visa programs for Americans relocating abroad in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-golden-visa-programs-americans-relocating-abroad-2026/
Published: 2026-10-07

Best golden visa programs for Americans in 2026: Greece, Portugal, Italy, Cyprus and Malta compared, plus what the Spain closure means and what to confirm first.

Q: Is Spain's golden visa still available in 2026?
A: No. Spain ended its golden visa for new applicants in April 2025. Guides that still list it are out of date, so confirm current options with an immigration professional.

Q: Can Americans still get a Portuguese golden visa in 2026?
A: The real estate route ended in 2023, but fund-based and cultural contribution routes are reported as available. Confirm current rules and thresholds before you plan around them.

Q: Does a golden visa make me a citizen?
A: No. A golden visa is a residence permit. Citizenship is a separate process with its own requirements, and not every program leads to it.

Q: Do I still file U.S. taxes if I get a golden visa?
A: U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax filing rules wherever they live. A residence permit does not change that, so get cross-border tax advice before you invest.

Q: How much does a golden visa cost?
A: It depends on the country, route and location, and figures change. Beyond the investment itself, budget for legal fees, taxes, due diligence and any ongoing costs.

Q: Can a golden visa replace a retirement or remote-work visa?
A: Sometimes, but not automatically. Compare what each route requires in terms of presence, income and activity before choosing the one that fits your plan.

Q: Can relocation coaching replace an immigration lawyer?
A: No. Global Systems Studio's ROS™ relocation coaching coordinates planning decisions; qualified immigration, tax and financial professionals provide advice within their respective regulated fields.

## Best countries for Americans to retire abroad in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-countries-americans-retire-abroad-2026/

Best countries for Americans to retire abroad: Mexico leads for U.S. proximity. Compare five options and sequence residency, healthcare, finances and housing.

Q: What's the best country for Americans to retire abroad in 2026?
A: Mexico is this shortlist's default for Americans who prioritize geographic proximity to the United States. Portugal, Panama, Costa Rica and Spain fit different priorities; eligibility and healthcare arrangements determine whether a choice works for your household.

Q: Is Portugal better than Mexico for American retirees?
A: Portugal fits retirees committed to a European base; Mexico fits retirees prioritizing proximity to the United States. Compare the residence route, healthcare arrangements and return logistics for your household rather than treating either country as universally better.

Q: Can I retire abroad while keeping my U.S. citizenship?
A: Living abroad does not by itself require you to give up U.S. citizenship. U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax filing rules while abroad, so destination residence and U.S. obligations need separate assessment.

Q: Will Medicare cover me when I retire abroad?
A: Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States, apart from limited exceptions. Confirm the rules that apply to your circumstances and arrange destination coverage and any transition coverage separately.

Q: Can I work remotely on Spain's non-lucrative residence route?
A: Do not use Spain's non-lucrative route as a remote-work plan. It restricts work; ask a qualified immigration professional to assess your intended activity and identify a suitable route before applying.

Q: Should I sign a lease before applying for retirement residence?
A: Confirm the residence route's housing-evidence requirements before signing a lease. Some application processes require accommodation evidence, but the commitment and cancellation terms still need assessment against your application sequence.

Q: Can relocation coaching replace an immigration lawyer or tax advisor?
A: No. Global Systems Studio's ROS™ relocation coaching coordinates planning decisions; qualified immigration, tax and financial professionals provide advice within their respective regulated fields.

## Best European countries for Americans to retire abroad in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-european-countries-americans-retire-abroad-2026/

The best European countries for Americans to retire abroad depend on residency, taxes and healthcare. Compare five options and plan the move in the right order.

Q: What's the best European country for an American retiree in 2026?
A: Portugal is the default starting point in this shortlist for retirees assessing passive-income residence. The best individual choice depends on residence eligibility, finances, healthcare and housing; no country wins for every household.

Q: Is Portugal better than Spain for American retirees?
A: Portugal and Spain fit different residence-planning questions. Portugal's D7 route is a starting point for qualifying passive-income applicants, while Spain's non-lucrative route is relevant to a nonworking retirement plan. Have an immigration professional assess your circumstances before choosing.

Q: Can I retire in Europe using only tourist permission?
A: Tourist permission is not long-term residence permission. For U.S. visitors, the standard Schengen short-stay allowance is up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area, not a fresh allowance in each country. Long-term retirement requires the appropriate residence route.

Q: Will Medicare cover my healthcare after I move to Europe?
A: Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States, with limited exceptions. Arrange appropriate overseas coverage and verify any public-system eligibility before departure. Prescription continuity needs its own plan.

Q: Do Americans still file U.S. taxes after retiring abroad?
A: U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax rules on worldwide income while living abroad. Filing requirements depend on individual circumstances, and foreign account reporting can also apply. A qualified cross-border tax professional should assess both countries' obligations.

Q: Should I buy a home before applying for retirement residence?
A: Do not make a property purchase your first step. Establish residence eligibility and accommodation-evidence requirements, then obtain local contract advice before committing. Property ownership and permission to reside are separate questions.

Q: Can Global Systems Studio handle my immigration and tax decisions?
A: Global Systems Studio provides destination-independent relocation coaching and consulting through ROS™, not individualized legal, tax or investment advice. ROS™ can coordinate the planning sequence; qualified specialists must answer the regulated professional questions.

## Best 7 expat financial advisors for Americans in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/best-expat-financial-advisors-americans-2026/

Choose an expat financial advisor by need: cross-border planning, U.S. taxes, investments or relocation. Compare seven advisor types and their limits in 2026.

Q: What's the best expat financial advisor for Americans?
A: A cross-border financial planner is the default choice when you need coordinated financial decisions across countries. For a defined tax, investment or legal problem, choose the specialist qualified to address it.

Q: Do Americans abroad still need to file U.S. taxes?
A: Living abroad does not automatically remove U.S. filing obligations. U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax on worldwide income; filing requirements depend on their circumstances.

Q: Is a CPA better than an enrolled agent for expats?
A: Neither credential alone establishes the better fit. Compare relevant international experience, the services included and whether you need return preparation, IRS representation or broader accounting work.

Q: Does spending 330 days abroad eliminate U.S. tax?
A: No. IRS Publication 54 describes a physical presence test requiring at least 330 full days in foreign countries during a consecutive 12-month period, but meeting that test does not itself eliminate all U.S. tax or filing obligations.

Q: Can my existing investment adviser serve me overseas?
A: Your adviser must confirm whether the firm can serve residents of your destination. Check that before assuming your existing investment relationship can continue unchanged.

Q: Is Global Systems Studio an expat financial advisor?
A: Global Systems Studio is described as a relocation coaching and consulting provider offering ROS™. Its stated scope covers planning legal, financial, housing and healthcare steps; use qualified specialists for regulated advice and professional filings.

Q: What should I ask an advisor before relocating in 2026?
A: Ask which jurisdictions the advisor covers, what deliverables you receive and which questions are excluded. Also establish who coordinates with your U.S. and destination-country specialists.

## Can digital nomads qualify for the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/can-digital-nomads-qualify-for-feie-2026/

Digital nomads can qualify for the FEIE with the physical presence test, but a tax home abroad is required. See who qualifies and what the exclusion does not cover.

Q: Can digital nomads claim the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion?
A: Yes, if they have a foreign tax home and meet the bona fide residence or physical presence test. Most nomads use the physical presence test.

Q: Do my 330 days have to be in one country?
A: No. The 330 full days can be spread across different foreign countries within a 12-month period.

Q: Do days in the air count?
A: Time spent in international airspace or waters generally does not count as time in a foreign country, so allow for it in your count.

Q: Does the exclusion remove self-employment tax?
A: Generally no. It reduces income tax on earned income but usually leaves self-employment tax in place.

Q: What if I visit the United States for a month?
A: U.S. days do not count toward the 330, so a long visit can make the test harder to pass. Plan trips home against your 12-month window.

Q: Is this tax advice?
A: No. This is educational context. Confirm your own situation with a qualified cross-border tax professional.

## Can you keep contributing to a 529 plan while living abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/contribute-to-529-plan-while-living-abroad-2026/

Yes, many Americans abroad can keep funding a 529 plan, and it can pay for eligible foreign schools. See provider rules, qualified expenses and tax caveats for 2026.

Q: Can I open or keep a 529 plan if I live abroad?
A: Often yes, but providers set their own rules on foreign addresses and funding. Ask yours directly.

Q: Can I use a 529 at a foreign university?
A: Potentially, if the school is an eligible institution under U.S. rules. Verify the school before you withdraw.

Q: Will my new country tax the 529?
A: It might. Local tax treatment varies, so get local advice.

Q: Do I still get a state tax deduction?
A: Only if your state offers one and you still owe tax there. Check with the state or your adviser.

Q: What if my child does not use the money for college?
A: You can generally change the beneficiary, or take a non-qualified withdrawal, which can carry tax on earnings and an additional tax.

Q: Is this tax advice?
A: Confirm your situation with a qualified cross-border tax or legal professional before acting.

## The Disconnection Nobody Prepares You For
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/disconnection-nobody-prepares-you-for/

Your children are in the U.S. Your grandchildren are in the U.S. The grief of leaving that behind is real: and nobody in the relocation space talks about it honestly.

## Do you still pay US taxes working remotely from abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/do-you-still-pay-us-taxes-working-remotely-abroad-2026/

Yes, U.S. citizens generally owe U.S. tax on worldwide income while working remotely abroad. See which exclusions, credits and filings apply in 2026.

Q: Do I still file a U.S. tax return if I work remotely from abroad?
A: Yes. U.S. citizens and green card holders generally must file regardless of where they live or work, though the filing deadline is extended for many taxpayers abroad.

Q: Does the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion cover all my remote income?
A: No. It covers earned income only, up to an annual limit, and only if you qualify. It does not cover investment income, pensions or Social Security.

Q: Do I owe self-employment tax if I use the exclusion?
A: Often yes. The exclusion reduces income tax, but self-employment tax generally still applies unless a totalization agreement removes it.

Q: Can I use the exclusion and the Foreign Tax Credit together?
A: You can use both in the same year, but not on the same dollars of income. Which one fits better depends on your income mix and the foreign tax you pay.

Q: Will my U.S. state still tax me?
A: It can. Rules differ by state, and some expect you to take specific steps to end residency. Check your state before you leave.

Q: Is this tax advice?
A: No. This is educational context. Confirm your situation with a qualified cross-border tax professional before filing or making commitments.

## How long before you lose state residency when living abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/how-long-before-you-lose-state-residency-living-abroad-2026/

There is no single timeline for ending U.S. state residency when you move abroad. See how domicile works, which states are strict and what to do before you leave.

Q: How many days abroad end my state residency?
A: No single number applies. States look at domicile, intent and ties, and some add statutory day-count rules.

Q: Can my state still tax me after I move abroad?
A: Yes, if it still treats you as a resident or taxes income sourced to the state. A documented change of domicile helps.

Q: Does keeping my house matter?
A: Yes. A home available for your use is one of the strongest ties a state can point to.

Q: Do I file a final state return?
A: Many states expect a part-year or final resident return. Check your state's rules for the year you leave.

Q: Can I vote in my old state from abroad?
A: U.S. citizens abroad can generally vote absentee in federal elections, but doing so can affect residency evidence in some states. Check first.

Q: Is this tax advice?
A: Confirm your situation with a qualified cross-border tax or legal professional before acting.

## How long can Americans stay abroad without a visa in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/how-long-can-americans-stay-abroad-without-a-visa-2026/

Visa-free stays for Americans range from about 30 to 180 days depending on the country. See common limits, why they differ and how to plan beyond them.

Q: How many days can an American stay without a visa?
A: It depends on the country, commonly from about 30 to 90 days, sometimes longer. Check the official source.

Q: What is the Schengen 90/180 rule?
A: You can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period across Schengen countries combined for short visits.

Q: Can I leave and re-enter to reset the clock?
A: Not safely. Many countries count days in a way that does not allow resets, and repeated visits can lead to refusal of entry.

Q: Can I work remotely on a tourist stay?
A: Rules differ and many tourist statuses do not allow work. Check before you do.

Q: Do I need an electronic authorization?
A: Some destinations require one. Check current entry requirements before you book.

Q: Is this immigration advice?
A: Confirm your situation with a qualified professional before acting.

## How long does it take to get a digital nomad visa in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/how-long-does-it-take-to-get-a-digital-nomad-visa-2026/

Digital nomad visa processing times range from days to several months, depending on the country and your documents. See what drives the timeline and how to prepare.

Q: How long does a digital nomad visa take?
A: From days to several months, depending on the country and your documents. Check the official source for your destination.

Q: What slows applications down?
A: Missing or expired documents, apostille and translation delays and consulate appointment availability.

Q: Do I need health insurance?
A: Many programs require it. Confirm the exact requirements for your destination.

Q: Can I work for U.S. clients on the visa?
A: Programs are generally designed for remote work for non-local clients. Read the terms of your specific visa.

Q: Does the visa make me a tax resident?
A: Not by itself, but staying long enough can create local tax residency. Get advice.

Q: Is this immigration advice?

## How much does it cost to relocate internationally in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/how-much-does-it-cost-to-relocate-internationally-2026/

International relocation costs vary widely by destination, household and visa. See the cost categories, a planning worksheet and the expenses people forget in 2026.

Q: How much does it cost to move abroad?
A: It varies with destination, household size and visa route. Build a category budget from quotes and add a reserve.

Q: What costs do people forget?
A: Overlap rent, document and translation costs, renewals, currency conversion spreads and the time before income starts.

Q: Is it cheaper to ship belongings or buy new?
A: It depends on volume and the destination. Many movers find that shipping less and buying locally works out better.

Q: How much cushion should I keep?
A: Enough to cover living costs for the period you will be settling, plus delays. Your timeline and income type determine the number.

Q: Can I deduct international moving costs?
A: Federal moving expense deductions are generally limited by current law, with exceptions for certain members of the Armed Forces. Check with a tax professional.

Q: Is this financial advice?
A: No. This is educational context. Work with a qualified professional for your situation.

## How much money do you need to retire abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/how-much-money-do-you-need-to-retire-abroad-2026/

There is no single number to retire abroad. Build one from your destination budget, healthcare, taxes and a cushion. See a step-by-step method and worked example.

Q: How much do I need to retire abroad?
A: It depends on your destination, healthcare, taxes and income. Build a city-level budget, subtract reliable income and size savings to cover the gap with a cushion.

Q: Can I live on Social Security alone abroad?
A: Some people can in low-cost areas, but it depends on your benefit amount, healthcare and visa requirements. Do not assume it works without a budget.

Q: Does Medicare work abroad?
A: Generally no. Medicare does not usually cover care outside the United States, so plan separate coverage.

Q: Is the 4% rule reliable?
A: It is a rough starting point, not a guarantee. Your age, taxes, investments and currency exposure can change what is sustainable.

Q: Should I rent before buying abroad?
A: Many advisers suggest renting first so you can test the city, season and budget before a larger commitment.

Q: Is this financial advice?
A: No. This is educational context. Work with a qualified financial professional for a personal plan.

## How much savings should you have before moving abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/how-much-savings-before-moving-abroad-2026/

There is no universal savings target for moving abroad. Size yours from your destination budget, runway months and visa requirements. See a practical method for 2026.

Q: How much should I save before moving abroad?
A: Cover one-time move costs, a runway of living expenses and a reserve, and check any visa financial requirements.

Q: How long should my runway be?
A: It depends on whether you have income. A job search or new business usually calls for a longer runway.

Q: Should I keep savings in dollars or local currency?
A: Many people hold some of each. The right mix depends on where your income and spending are.

Q: Can my savings affect my visa?
A: Yes. Some visas require proof of a minimum balance or income, sometimes held for a set period.

Q: Should I wait until I have more saved?
A: Waiting has costs too. Compare the risk of moving underfunded with the cost of delay, and consider a smaller trial stay first.

Q: Is this financial advice?
A: No. This is educational context. Work with a qualified professional for your situation.

## Can you still contribute to an HSA while living abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/hsa-contributions-while-living-abroad-2026/

You can keep an HSA abroad, but contributions require qualifying high-deductible health coverage. See the 2026 limits, the foreign insurance problem and what stays tax-free.

Q: Can I keep my HSA if I move abroad?
A: Usually yes. Check that your provider will service the account with a foreign address.

Q: Can I keep contributing to an HSA from abroad?
A: Only if you are covered by an HSA-eligible high-deductible plan and have no disqualifying coverage. Many foreign plans do not qualify.

Q: Can I use my HSA for medical care abroad?
A: Qualified medical expenses are generally eligible, including care received abroad, with documentation kept.

Q: What are the 2026 contribution limits?
A: $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage, with an additional $1,000 for people 55 or older. Confirm on IRS guidance.

Q: What if I over-contribute?
A: Excess contributions should be corrected following IRS rules. Ask your tax professional promptly.

Q: Is this tax advice?
A: Confirm your situation with a qualified cross-border tax or legal professional before acting.

## Is it cheaper to retire abroad than in the US in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/is-it-cheaper-to-retire-abroad-than-in-the-us-2026/

Often, but not always. Housing and daily costs can be lower abroad, while healthcare, flights and taxes can offset the savings. See how to compare your real numbers.

Q: Is it really cheaper to retire abroad?
A: Often for housing and daily costs, but healthcare, travel, taxes and currency can reduce the gap. Compare your own budget in both places.

Q: Which costs are most often underestimated?
A: Healthcare, flights home, visa renewals and the cost of living in expat-friendly neighborhoods.

Q: Do I still pay U.S. taxes if I retire abroad?
A: U.S. citizens generally remain subject to U.S. tax on worldwide income, so retirement income can still be taxed, and local taxes may apply too.

Q: Does Social Security pay abroad?
A: It can be paid to many countries, but there are restrictions in some. Check with the Social Security Administration for your destination.

Q: How do I test a destination before moving?
A: Rent short term in the season you will live there and track your actual spending.

## Can you keep your US driver's license while living abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/keep-us-drivers-license-living-abroad-2026/

You can usually keep a valid U.S. license until it expires, but renewing from abroad is harder. See how international driving permits work and when to convert to a local license.

Q: Can I drive abroad with my U.S. license?
A: Often for a limited period, usually with an International Driving Permit. Check the destination's rules.

Q: Can I renew my license from abroad?
A: It depends on the state. Some allow mail or online renewal, others require an in-person visit.

Q: What is an International Driving Permit?
A: A translation of your license that you generally get before you leave. It is not valid alone.

Q: Do I need a local license as a resident?
A: Many countries require it after a set period. Check the deadline and whether an exchange is possible.

Q: Does keeping my license affect state residency?

## Can you keep your US-based LLC if you move abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/keep-us-llc-if-you-move-abroad-2026/

Yes, you can generally keep a U.S. LLC after you move abroad, but taxes, the registered agent and local rules still apply. See what changes and what to check first.

Q: Do I have to close my LLC if I move abroad?
A: Generally no. A U.S. LLC can continue to exist while its owner lives elsewhere, as long as state requirements are met.

Q: Do I still need a registered agent?
A: Yes. The LLC needs a U.S. registered agent in its formation state to receive official notices.

Q: Does the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion cover my LLC income?
A: It can apply to earned income if you qualify, but it generally does not remove self-employment tax and does not cover passive income.

Q: Will my new country tax my U.S. LLC?
A: Possibly. Local rules on foreign companies and residents vary, so get local advice before you operate from there.

Q: Can I keep my U.S. business bank account?
A: Often, but banks differ in how they treat foreign owner addresses. Ask before you update the address.

Q: Is this legal or tax advice?
A: Confirm your situation with a qualified cross-border tax or legal professional before acting.

## Can you relocate abroad and keep your US citizenship in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/relocate-abroad-and-keep-us-citizenship-2026/

Yes. Moving abroad does not affect your U.S. citizenship, and you can live overseas for life. See what stays the same, what changes and how dual citizenship works.

Q: Do I lose my U.S. citizenship if I live abroad?
A: No. Only a formal renunciation ends it.

Q: Can I hold dual citizenship?
A: U.S. law generally allows it, but check the other country's rules.

Q: Do I still pay U.S. taxes?
A: U.S. citizens generally file U.S. returns on worldwide income, with credits and exclusions that may reduce tax.

Q: Can I vote from abroad?
A: Citizens abroad can generally vote absentee in federal elections.

Q: Can I renew my passport overseas?
A: Generally yes, through a U.S. embassy or consulate, or by mail if you qualify.

Q: Can I defer my loans because I move abroad?

## Countries to retire abroad ranked by cost of living in 2026
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/retire-abroad-countries-ranked-cost-of-living-2026/

Countries to retire abroad ranked by cost of living need local budgets. Compare five destinations, then check residency, healthcare, housing, and U.S. taxes.

Q: What are the best countries to retire abroad ranked by cost of living?
A: A useful ranking compares equivalent city-level housing, healthcare, and household needs rather than national averages alone. Mexico, Portugal, Costa Rica, Panama, and Malaysia are comparison candidates with different planning advantages, not a verified cheapest-to-most-expensive order.

Q: Is Mexico better than Portugal for an American retiree?
A: Mexico fits a North American location preference; Portugal fits a European-base preference. Your residence eligibility, healthcare requirements, and city-level budget determine which destination fits your retirement.

Q: How much does retiring abroad cost?
A: Retiring abroad requires a household-specific budget covering housing, healthcare, daily living, retained U.S. obligations, and relocation expenses. Separate recurring spending from move-related spending before comparing destinations.

Q: Can I retire in Portugal using the visitor allowance?
A: A visitor allowance is not permission to establish indefinite residence in Portugal. The general Schengen short-stay rule for U.S. citizens is 90 days within any 180-day period; confirm the residence route appropriate to your circumstances.

Q: Will Medicare cover me when I retire abroad?
A: Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States, subject to limited exceptions. Eligibility commonly begins at age 65 years, but eligibility and overseas coverage are separate questions; verify your coverage and arrange destination-appropriate care.

Q: Do I still have U.S. tax responsibilities after moving abroad?
A: Moving abroad does not automatically end U.S. federal tax responsibilities for U.S. citizens. Filing, reporting, treaty provisions, and relief depend on your circumstances, so consult a qualified cross-border tax professional.

Q: Can Global Systems Studio give me country-specific legal advice?
A: Global Systems Studio provides destination-independent relocation planning through ROS™, not country-specific legal advice. Its courses, guidebooks, and 1:1 sessions help coordinate decisions; qualified specialists address immigration, tax, and other regulated questions.

## Can you still invest in a Roth IRA while living abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/roth-ira-contributions-while-living-abroad-2026/

You can often still fund a Roth IRA abroad, but income excluded under the FEIE does not count. Learn the compensation rule, income limits and custodian issues.

Q: Can I contribute to a Roth IRA if I live abroad?
A: Often yes, if you have eligible U.S. taxable compensation and your income is within the Roth limits, and your custodian accepts you at a foreign address.

Q: Does the FEIE affect my IRA eligibility?
A: Yes. Income you exclude with the FEIE generally does not count as compensation, so excluding everything can leave you with no room to contribute.

Q: What if I contribute too much by mistake?
A: An excess contribution can face a yearly penalty until corrected, so remove or recharacterize it with help from a qualified professional.

Q: Will my foreign country tax my Roth IRA?
A: Some countries do not treat a Roth as tax free, and a tax treaty may or may not help. Check the rules where you will be a tax resident.

Q: Can I keep my existing IRA if I move abroad?
A: Usually, but providers differ on foreign addresses. Ask your custodian what they allow before you change your mailing address.

Q: Is this investment or tax advice?
A: No. This is educational context. Confirm limits and eligibility with a qualified cross-border tax professional.

## Can you transfer a US 401(k) into a foreign pension plan in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/transfer-us-401k-to-foreign-pension-plan-2026/

A U.S. 401(k) generally cannot be moved tax-free into a foreign pension plan. See the safer options, the tax risks and what to ask before you move retirement money abroad.

Q: Can I roll a 401(k) into a foreign pension plan tax-free?
A: Generally no. Foreign pension plans are not typically qualified U.S. retirement plans, so a transfer is usually treated as a taxable distribution.

Q: Can I keep my 401(k) after I move abroad?
A: Often yes, but your plan or custodian may restrict accounts tied to a foreign address. Ask the provider before you update your address.

Q: Is there a penalty for early withdrawal if I live abroad?
A: Moving abroad does not by itself remove the 10% additional tax on early distributions. Exceptions exist but depend on the facts.

Q: Will my new country tax my 401(k)?
A: Possibly. It depends on local law and any tax treaty with the United States. Get local advice before you take distributions.

Q: Should I convert to a Roth before I move?
A: It depends on your tax bracket now and later, how your destination treats Roth accounts and whether you can pay the tax from other funds.

Q: Is this tax advice?

## Can you still get a US credit card after moving abroad in 2026?
URL: https://globalsystemsstudio.com/blog/us-credit-card-after-moving-abroad-2026/

You can often keep US credit cards abroad, but new approvals are harder without a US address. See how to protect your credit, what issuers ask and what to do before you leave.

Q: Can I keep my U.S. credit card if I live abroad?
A: Often yes, but issuers vary. Tell your issuer how to contact you and check their terms on foreign addresses.

Q: Can I apply for a new U.S. card from abroad?
A: It is harder. Most require a U.S. address and credit file. Apply before you leave if you can.

Q: Will my U.S. credit score carry to my new country?
A: No. Credit files are generally country-specific, so you will build a local history there.

Q: Should I close cards I do not use?
A: Closing old accounts can shorten your credit history. Keep the oldest open with a small recurring charge if you can.

Q: How do I avoid foreign transaction fees?
A: Use cards that do not charge them and pay in local currency when prompted.
